title: 10 Easy Ways to Save Money
summary: Live-recorded advice episode of Stuff You Should Know on ten easy ways to save money. The hosts cover cutting waste and entertainment subscriptions, gym memberships, car fuel efficiency and tire inflation, grocery shopping habits and loyalty programs, generic drugs, quitting smoking, household energy use and vampire power, health insurance versus hospital costs, cell phone plans, avoiding credit card interest, waiting before purchases, building an emergency fund, paying yourself first, CDs, direct stock purchase plans, index funds, discount brokerages, and 401(k) matching. The episode ends with a listener mail about the earlier death-and-dying episode and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening and framing
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the live recording and the advice format, and argue that saving money is a basis for a conscientious, financially independent lifestyle, not just for the rich.

segments.title: Savings targets and not comparing yourself to others
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a rule of thumb of saving about eight times your ending salary by age 65, with milestones at 30 and 40, and advise not to compare yourself to others.

segments.title: Cutting entertainment and gym costs
segments.summary: The hosts suggest trimming unused subscriptions such as cable, magazines and Netflix DVD delivery, and reconsidering gym memberships in favor of free outdoor running or equipment at parks.

segments.title: Car costs: fuel economy, insurance and tire pressure
segments.summary: The hosts compare fuel costs for 25 versus 15 mpg over 80,000 miles, suggest reviewing car insurance and raising deductibles, and note that underinflated tires waste gas.

segments.title: Grocery shopping, lunches and coupons
segments.summary: The hosts advise eating before shopping, packing lunches, planning meals around store specials and coupons, sticking to a list, and using store loyalty cards and gas rewards.

segments.title: Generic drugs and quitting smoking
segments.summary: The hosts recommend FDA-approved generic drugs over brand names, explain patents, and say quitting smoking saves thousands per year; they also mention cutting addictions like drinking.

segments.title: Household energy and vampire power
segments.summary: The hosts discuss reducing household energy use, standby power that costs money even when devices are off, energy monitoring devices, and Energy Star rebates.

segments.title: Health insurance versus hospital costs
segments.summary: Chuck explains that he skipped insurance in his twenties and argues that the cost of a hospital stay far exceeds years of premiums, so going uninsured is not a way to save. Josh and Chuck also discuss checking existing insurance coverage.

segments.title: Cell phone plans and tracking expenses
segments.summary: The hosts suggest reviewing cell phone plans and texting needs, and say the first step is to write down and track monthly expenses.

segments.title: Living debt free and waiting before purchases
segments.summary: The hosts describe paying credit cards in full to avoid finance charges, recommend a one-month waiting period before major purchases, and discuss 0% financing deals with caution.

segments.title: Emergency fund, debt payoff and investing basics
segments.summary: The hosts advise building a three-to-six-month emergency fund, paying off debt, paying yourself first, and then considering CDs, direct stock purchase plans, index funds, discount brokerages, and 401(k) matching.

segments.title: Closing
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up and encourage listeners to search for the episode and keep learning about finance.
